claims.text: On September 12, 2026, PDP President Mehbooba Mufti welcomed BRICS leaders' condemnation of the Pahalgam terror attack.
Mehbooba Mufti stated that India, as chair of BRICS, should have ensured the collective statement addressed devastation in Gaza and US-Israeli military action against Iran.
Mehbooba Mufti stated that civilian blood has no nationality and international justice cannot have double standards.
Mehbooba Mufti welcomed the BRICS declaration's support for humanitarian assistance to Gaza.
BRICS nations opposed unilateral trade measures such as the European Union's Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) in the New Delhi Declaration.
The European Union's Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) entered its operational regime on January 1, imposing a border tax on carbon-intensive goods such as iron, steel, aluminium, and cement.
Four BRICS member countries—Russia, Saudi Arabia, Iran, and the UAE—are major global exporters of fossil fuel.
COP31 is scheduled to take place in Turkey in November.
The 18th BRICS Summit took place in New Delhi under India's chairmanship.
The expanded BRICS alliance encompasses eleven full member states, including the UAE, Iran, Egypt, Ethiopia, Indonesia, and Saudi Arabia.
Chinese President Xi Jinping visited India for the BRICS summit, marking his first visit to India in seven years.
Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi announced that the 2026 BRICS New Delhi Declaration was adopted unanimously following overnight negotiations.

The BRICS New Delhi Declaration expressed grave concern over rising regional tensions in West Asia and called for maximum restraint, civilian protection, and a two-state solution based on pre-1967 borders.
Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian met Abu Dhabi's Crown Prince Khaled bin Mohamed Al Nahyan at the BRICS summit on September 12, 2026.
The talks between Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian and Crown Prince Khaled bin Mohamed Al Nahyan were their highest-level meeting since conflict began.
Bahrain refused to meet with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian at the BRICS summit.
BRICS nations unanimously approved the 45-page New Delhi Declaration at the summit led by India.
The New Delhi Declaration condemned an April 22, 2025 terror attack in Pahalgam, Jammu and Kashmir, which killed 26 people and injured many others.
The New Delhi Declaration condemned violations of the ceasefire in Lebanon and called on Israel to withdraw its occupying forces from Lebanese territory.
China and Russia reiterated their support for Brazil and India to play a greater role in the United Nations, including the UN Security Council.
Maratha quota activist Manoj Jarange announced a five-day march to Mumbai starting September 15.
Manoj Jarange announced he will launch an indefinite hunger strike at Azad Maidan in Mumbai on September 20.
The planned march route from Antarwali Sarati to Mumbai covers about 100 kilometres per day with scheduled halts at Patoda, Shrigonda, Hadapsar, and Khopoli.
Authorities deployed additional police personnel along with ambulance and fire brigade teams to Antarwali Sarati starting Saturday.
Manoj Jarange-Patil has been on an indefinite hunger strike since August 29 demanding job and education quotas for the Maratha community.
Manoj Jarange-Patil's demands include the issuance of Kunbi certificates to Marathas based on 5.8 million records.
Manoj Jarange-Patil requested Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis not to create barriers for the protesters.
Zahra Pezeshkian, daughter of Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, visited the Prime Minister Museum and the BRICS Bazaar in Delhi.
The Bombay High Court refused to issue orders restraining Maratha quota activist Manoj Jarange-Patil from holding a march to Mumbai.
A division bench of Chief Justice Mahesh Chandra Tripathi and Justice Advait M Sethna heard a petition filed by Mumbai resident Nilesh Dhanukar seeking to stop the march.
Advocate General Milind Sathe told the court that Manoj Jarange-Patil had not sought permission under the 2025 Public Meeting, Agitation and Procession Rules to hold the march to Mumbai.
